thread.title: Apple bonds downgraded by CreditSights on concerns about China trade tensions

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Apple bonds downgraded by CreditSights on concerns about China trade tensions
text:
Research and data firm CreditSights preemptively downgraded its recommendation on bonds issued by Apple Inc.
 AAPL, -0.63%
 on Tuesday, and said it expects the escalating trade tensions between China and the U.S. to have an outsize impact on the iPhone maker relative to its peers. Analyst Jordan Chalfin cut his rating to underperform from market perform. While near-term operating trends should benefit from higher average selling prices and growth in services, Apple could underperform its A-rated tech peers if current tensions persist, Chalfin wrote in a note. Trump has said he expects to move ahead with raising tariffs on $200 billion of Chinese goods to 25% from 10% on Jan. 1. “We would avoid Apple’s longer dated bonds, as its massive cash hoard and market cap provide a margin of safety for the near-to-medium term,” Chalfin wrote. Apple was already under pressure from reports of weaker-than-expected demand for new iPhone models and the company cut the price of the iPhone XR for carried-subsidized contracts in Japan, he said. Spreads on Apple’s 3.75% notes that mature in November of 2047 widened by 8 basis points in afternoon trade to 107 basis points over Treasurys, according to MarketAxess. The notes were trading at 89 cents on the dollar. The 3.850% notes that mature in May of 2043 were 5 basis points wider on the week at 106 basis points over Treasurys. In equities, Apple shares were down 0.7% but have gained 2.4% in 2018, while the S&P 500
 SPX, -0.02%
 has fallen 0.01%.
